title: Hosted API long-tail token econ mapping
content:
Purpose:
- Quick experimental workbook to map the long-tail of Hosted API requests into cost buckets by model and region. Goal is to surface marginal per-token cost for low-frequency requests and propose low-friction mitigations (small-model fallbacks, longer batching windows, regional routing).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Top 10% of requests (high qps customers) drive ~65% of tokens and have predictable COGS.
- Long tail (requests ranked 50–99 percentile) are ~30% of tokens but >80% of request count — they inflate orchestration and tail GPU utilization.
- Marginal per-token cost in the long-tail (small batches, 1–3 requests) can be 3x–7x higher than bulk slices due to GPU cold-starts, low packing, and higher per-request overheads.

Workbook layout (sheet tabs recommended):
1) bucketed-econ-view - primary table
   Columns: Bucket | Pctl_range | Avg_seq_len | Avg_tokens_req | Req_share_pct | Req_count_est | Model_family | Region | Est_gpu_hours/month | COGS_per_1k_reqs | Marginal_per_token | Notes | Suggested_action

   Sample rows (numbers are illustrative):
   - head | 0-10% | 120 | 540 | 65% | 1,200,000 | mix-gptx | us-west1 | 2,400 | $8.40 | $0.0016 | stable high-util | keep reserved pool
   - mid  | 10-50% | 64  | 180 | 22% | 4,000,000 | mix-gptx | us-east1 | 1,100 | $2.90 | $0.0009 | opportunistic batching | enable 20ms pack
   - tail | 50-99% | 32  | 42  | 13% | 9,000,000 | small/ft | eu-west1 | 600 | $6.20 | $0.0048 | lots of cold starts | evaluate tiny-model fallback
   - nano | 90-99.9% | 8  | 12  | 3% | 12,000,000 | tiny-llm | ap-south1 | 150 | $18.00 | $0.0125 | huge overhead | edge caching + fallback

   Formulas (text):
   - Est_gpu_hours/month = (Tokens_per_month_by_bucket / avg_tokens_per_gpu_hour) + orchestration_hours_overhead
   - COGS_per_1k_reqs = (Est_gpu_hours * infra_hourly_rate + infra_fixed_ops) / (Req_count_est / 1000) + network + storage amortization
   - Marginal_per_token = COGS_per_1k_reqs / (Avg_tokens_req * 1000)

2) regional-breakdown - split same buckets by region and model variant (eu/na/apac). Includes exchange rate adjustments and regional egress differences.

3) action-sim - quick what-if toggles: small-model-fallback-uptake_pct | batch-window_ms | cache-hit_rate | route-to-dedicated_pct -> outputs delta COGS and delta latency.

Key tradeoffs surfaced so far (notes):
- Increasing pack window from 10ms -> 50ms reduces marginal per-token in tail by ~18–25% for our sample workload but increases 95p latency by ~8–12ms.
- Tiny-model fallback (quantized 4-bit) for requests <20 tokens reduces tail GPU hours by 40% in simulations but requires 2% quality regression monitoring and infra + storage ops (~$5k/mo) to maintain model variants.
- Regional routing: routing tail requests to lower-cost regions gives near-term COGS wins but adds data sovereignty and latency complexity; recommended for non-sensitive workloads only.

Suggested immediate experiments (priority + owner):
- EXP-1: 30-day pack-window A/B (owner: Ethan). Measure token-cost delta and 95p latency per customer segment. (Jira: PLAT-2143)
- EXP-2: Tiny-model fallback pilot for <16-token requests (owner: Lina). Deploy in eu-west1 only, sample 3% traffic, compare quality vs cost.
- EXP-3: Regional tail routing TTL flags (owner: Noah). Prove routing rule for non-PII buckets; track compliance and latencies.

Open questions / To-do:
- Need tighter estimate for orchestration overhead (container spin-up time distribution by region). SRE to provide metrics.
- Validate avg_tokens_per_gpu_hour per model family (Research to provide real benchmark numbers, current sheet uses proxies).
- Business: how much margin shrink is acceptable for customer segments under PLG? (cc: Revenue Ops)

Notes for follow-ups:
- Convert sample rows into a pivot-friendly long table and add a tiny Monte Carlo (sheet tab) for sensitivity over token length distributions.
- Add a per-customer view to identify which individual tenants are causing disproportionate long-tail infra costs.

Rough runbook links and references:
- PLAT-2143 (Jira): pilot steps for packing window experiment
- Confluence: OPT-LongTail-Econ (design notes)
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 (routing flags + tiny-model rollout)

End of draft — this is intentionally sketchy. Use this as a working spreadsheet to capture measured values over the next 2 weeks, then convert selected mitigations into prioritized product tickets.

Unresolved: who will own the tiny-model quantization ops? Ops or Research? put in triage meeting.
